cards.definitions: For n≥1 and S⊆[n], put χ_S(x)=∏_{i∈S}x_i, with χ_∅=1. The Fourier coefficient is f̂(S)=2^{−n}∑_{x∈{−1,1}^n}f(x)χ_S(x), so f=∑_{S⊆[n]}f̂(S)χ_S. The support is supp(f̂)={S:f̂(S)≠0}, and k(f)=|supp(f̂)|. It is at least one. Identify a subset S with its incidence vector in F₂^n and define r(f)=dim_{F₂} span{1_S:S∈supp(f̂)}. The empty set contributes the zero vector; it may count towards k but never increases r. This rank is not a real linear-span dimension of functions. The limit r(f_j)=ω(√k(f_j)) means that for every real M>0, the ratio eventually exceeds M. No bound on n_j in terms of j, explicit construction algorithm, or computational efficiency is requested. The negation is the existence of a universal constant C such that r(f)≤C√k(f) for every n and every such f. Since r(f)≤k(f), unbounded ratios necessarily require unbounded sparsities.
cards.answer_criterion: A positive answer must prove the existence of functions with unbounded r(f)/√k(f), equivalently a sequence with the displayed limits. A negative answer must prove a universal constant-factor square-root bound for every Boolean function. A fixed larger constant, finitely many examples, or a bound retaining a growing logarithmic factor does not decide the question.

cards.title: Black-box PIT from weighted SOS hardness
cards.formal: Does the existence of an explicit SOS-hard polynomial family in the sense of the ITCS 2021 source imply a deterministic polynomial-time blackbox polynomial identity test for general arithmetic circuits of polynomially bounded degree? The original hardness hypothesis is: for some fixed number N≥1 of variables, an explicit family (f_d) of degree d satisfies S_F(f_d)≥c d^{N(1/2+ε(d))} for all sufficiently large d, where c>0 is constant, ε(d)→0, and ε(d)/√(log log d/log d)→∞. The desired conclusion is full polynomial-time derandomization, not just subexponential or quasipolynomial time. Field, coefficient and exact cost conventions are not yet fixed to a single self-contained model.

cards.definitions: For a polynomial f over a field F of characteristic different from two, S_F(f) is the minimum of ∑ᵢ|supp(gᵢ)| over all finite identities f=∑ᵢcᵢgᵢ² with cᵢ∈F and gᵢ∈F[x₁,…,x_N]. supp(g) is the set of monomials with nonzero coefficient. Weights may be negative when F is ordered; this is a weighted algebraic sum of squares, not a nonnegative-polynomial certificate. There is no bound on the number of summands or on their degrees in the definition of S_F. A monomial appearing in several gᵢ is counted separately in each. The source’s explicitness condition requires coefficient encodings of length polynomial in d and a uniform algorithm that, on binary d, a monomial exponent tuple and a coefficient-bit position, returns that bit in time polynomial in log d for valid positions. The field and bit encoding must be specified to make this exact. N is fixed independently of d; constants in the hardness and explicitness bounds may depend on the family. Arithmetic circuits here are finite directed acyclic computations with variables and field constants at the leaves and binary addition and multiplication gates. Polynomial identity testing asks whether the resulting formal polynomial is identically zero. In the blackbox version, the algorithm knows bounds on the circuit size s, number of variables n and degree D, and accesses only exact evaluations. The requested polynomial-time dependence is in s,n,D, equivalently in a common bound t≥max{s,n,D}; it does not require polynomial time in log D. A hitting set is a finite set H of evaluation points such that every nonzero polynomial in the bounded circuit class is nonzero at some point of H. A deterministic construction of a polynomial-size hitting set in polynomial time would meet the blackbox target once field representation and operation costs are fixed.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove or refute the stated implication with the conference hardness hypothesis and a precisely fixed field/computational model. A positive answer must obtain deterministic polynomial-time blackbox PIT for unrestricted arithmetic circuits with the stated size and degree bounds. A sum-of-cubes hypothesis, a larger fixed hardness exponent, a change of the field allowed in decompositions, or merely subexponential/quasipolynomial PIT does not establish the requested implication.

cards.definitions: A binary constraint satisfaction instance has k variables, a finite alphabet Σ of size n, and explicitly given binary relations specifying the allowed pairs for constrained variable pairs. Its finite input length includes these relation tables. An assignment chooses one alphabet value for each variable; val(Π) is the maximum fraction of its constraints satisfied by an assignment. The promise is val(Π)=1 or val(Π)≤1−ε; no answer is prescribed for intermediate values. For an instance of encoded size L, fixed-parameter tractable means time f(k)L^C for some computable f and constant C independent of k and L. In the standard representation with one binary relation per constrained pair, this is equivalent to f(k)n^{O(1)} after absorbing polynomial k-factors into f. Here W[1]≠FPT is the standard deterministic hypothesis, equivalently that deciding whether a finite graph has a k-clique has no f(k)L^C algorithm. PIH asserts the existence of one fixed ε>0 for which the promised approximation task has no such algorithm, irrespective of the computable function f or constant exponent C. The question is the implication from exact parameterized hardness to that constant-gap hardness, not an unconditional assertion of W[1]≠FPT.
cards.answer_criterion: Establish the stated implication using only W[1]≠FPT as the complexity assumption, with a constant gap independent of k and n, or refute that implication. A result assuming ETH or Gap-ETH, a gap shrinking with k, or hardness for a list-assignment variant does not settle this target.

context_blocks.title: Finding one violated constraint is weaker than finding many
context_blocks.text: Exact unsatisfiability only says every assignment fails somewhere. PIH asks for a constant fraction of failures on every assignment. If an instance has many constraints, the existence of just one unavoidable violation need not give any fixed gap.

context_blocks.title: The parameter is the number of variables
context_blocks.text: The alphabet is allowed to grow with the input. Exhaustive search takes n^k time, whose exponent depends on k; that is not fixed-parameter tractable. A running time such as 2^{2^k}n^3 would qualify despite its very large dependence on k.

context_blocks.title: The source proves Baby PIH under the desired assumption
context_blocks.text: Baby PIH distinguishes satisfiable instances from instances for which even a constant-size list of values at each variable cannot satisfy every constraint. This is a different guarantee from saying that every ordinary assignment violates a constant fraction of constraints.

context_blocks.title: ETH already implies PIH
context_blocks.text: The Guruswami–Lin–Ren–Sun–Wu theorem derives PIH from the Exponential Time Hypothesis. ETH imposes a quantitative subexponential-time obstruction for 3SAT and is a stronger assumption than the parameterized separation sought here. The February 2026 survey still separates these targets.

The alphabet is allowed to grow with the input. Exhaustive search takes n^k time, whose exponent depends on k; that is not fixed-parameter tractable. A running time such as 2^{2^k}n^3 would qualify despite its very large dependence on k.

Baby PIH distinguishes satisfiable instances from instances for which even a constant-size list of values at each variable cannot satisfy every constraint. This is a different guarantee from saying that every ordinary assignment violates a constant fraction of constraints.

The Guruswami–Lin–Ren–Sun–Wu theorem derives PIH from the Exponential Time Hypothesis. ETH imposes a quantitative subexponential-time obstruction for 3SAT and is a stronger assumption than the parameterized separation sought here. The February 2026 survey still separates these targets.

cards.definitions: The input consists of the entries of the symmetric real tensor T∈(ℝᵈ)^{⊗4}; the individual aᵢ are hidden. Each aᵢ has independent coordinates of mean zero and variance 1/d, and all components are mutually independent. Let x₀ be uniform on the Euclidean sphere of radius √d and independent of these components. Define zₜ=T(I,xₜ₋₁,xₜ₋₁,xₜ₋₁)=Σᵢ⟨aᵢ,xₜ₋₁⟩³aᵢ and xₜ=√d·zₜ/‖zₜ‖₂. On the null event of a zero denominator, declare the run failed. No new tensor samples or independent noise are introduced between iterations. The same dynamics is normalized gradient ascent for S(x)=Σᵢ⟨aᵢ,x⟩⁴. The regime means integer sequences k=k(d) with k/d→∞ and k/d²→0 as d→∞; it is not restricted to k=d^c for a fixed exponent c. Directional error can be measured by min_{i,s∈{−1,+1}}‖xₜ/√d−s aᵢ/‖aᵢ‖₂‖₂, but the source does not specify its required size. Probability is over both the tensor components and the independent initial direction. The paper studies iteration counts with exact real arithmetic, not bit complexity of Gaussian input encodings. The target is recovery of one component; recovery of the entire decomposition is a different task.
cards.answer_criterion: A precise completion must give a recovery tolerance, success guarantee, stopping/output rule and the permitted parameter dependence of a polynomial iteration bound, then prove or refute that bound for the stated random model. A theorem that only shows the objective increasing, assumes an initially correlated component, or analyzes a planted single-spike tensor with Gaussian noise does not settle the source question.

context_blocks.title: Overcomplete means more components than dimensions
context_blocks.text: The tensor combines k hidden directions in ℝᵈ with k much larger than d. Randomness is imposed on the entire collection of directions, rather than on additive observation noise.

context_blocks.title: Random initialization can lead to a long delay
context_blocks.text: For d^{3/2}≪k≪d², Theorem 3.1 proves that all iterates up to T=o(k^{2/3}/(d(log k)^{1/3})) have vanishing normalized correlation with every component. For fixed k comparable to d^c with 3/2<c<2, this entails a polynomial delay.

context_blocks.title: A polynomial delay does not rule out polynomial recovery
context_blocks.text: The authors’ numerical evidence motivates eventual polynomial-time success. Their lower bound disproves an overly rapid convergence expectation, not that later polynomially many iterations can work.

context_blocks.title: The later tensor PCA theorem concerns different randomness
context_blocks.text: The 2024 paper gives a sharp positive analysis for one planted spike plus a tensor of independent Gaussian noise entries. That is not the overcomplete sum in this question, even though both use randomly initialized power iteration.

context_blocks.title: What still needs specification
context_blocks.text: The informal positive conjecture says “correctly learn” in polynomial time but does not prescribe the recovery error, its dependence on d and k, or a uniform polynomial iteration bound across all sequences d≪k≪d². A precise stopping/output convention is also needed if success means a returned iterate rather than visiting a good iterate. The normalized iteration and rank regime are recoverable, but an exact numerical error target or a polynomial-in-accuracy claim must not be invented.

references.title: Dynamic Complexity of Parity Exists Queries
references.authors: Vortmeier, Nils; Zeume, Thomas
references.locator: Unresolved-question passage on page 15; PDF page 15

cards.definitions: The domain D is a fixed finite set throughout a run; updates do not create or delete vertices. An element y is covered when at least one red predecessor x has an arc x→y. A covered vertex is counted once, regardless of how many red predecessors it has, and it need not itself be red. E is a binary relation, so loops are allowed; R is unary. The four update types are ins_E(u,v), del_E(u,v), ins_R(u), and del_R(u). Insertions of present tuples and deletions of absent tuples leave the input relation unchanged and are also allowed. A program chooses finitely many auxiliary relation symbols S, each of a fixed finite arity, including a distinguished zero-ary answer bit Ans. For each S and update type δ it supplies a first-order formula φ_{S,δ}(p̄;z̄), where p̄ are the changed tuple’s parameters and z̄ has the arity of S. The formula may use equality, the current input and auxiliary relations, Boolean connectives, and quantification over individual domain elements. It has no parity/counting quantifier, quantification over sets, function symbol or built-in numeric relation. After update δ(ā), each auxiliary relation becomes {b̄:(I,A)⊨φ_{S,δ}(ā;b̄)}, evaluated on the old input I and old auxiliary state A. All auxiliary updates occur simultaneously, alongside the specified input change. Empty initialization makes Ans false, correctly answering the empty covered set. The program’s formulas and arities are independent of |D| and of the update history. The number and arities of auxiliary relations are unrestricted finite constants chosen by the program; thus it may use polynomially many auxiliary bits, with its own fixed polynomial exponent. DynFO measures expressibility of these updates, rather than sequential constant-time execution of a formula on a Turing machine.
cards.answer_criterion: A positive answer is a finite collection of first-order update formulas and a proof of correctness from empty initialization for every finite domain and every finite update sequence. A negative answer must show that every such program, allowing arbitrary fixed auxiliary arities, fails on some domain and sequence. A lower bound only for quantifier-free formulas or a fixed arity, a program requiring unrestricted initial advice, or an algorithm for a bounded-degree variant does not settle the stated DynFO question.

cards.definitions: A polynomial family has fₙ∈F[x₁,…,x_{m(n)}], where m(n) and the total degree of fₙ are at most n^a+a for some fixed a. An algebraic formula is a finite rooted tree whose leaves are variables or constants in F and whose internal gates are binary addition or multiplication. Its output is a formal polynomial; equality means coefficientwise equality in F[x], also when F is finite. Its size is its number of nodes. An algebraic branching program is a finite directed acyclic graph with a designated source and sink and affine-linear polynomial labels on edges. It computes the sum, over all source-to-sink paths, of the product of the labels on that path. Count vertices, edges and the nonzero coefficients used to describe edge labels as its size; these choices differ only polynomially from the usual size conventions. Field constants have unit algebraic cost, with no bit-length bound. VF_F and VBP_F consist respectively of the polynomial families with formula size and branching-program size bounded by n^b+b for some constant b independent of n. These are nonuniform classes: a different finite computation may be chosen for each n, with no requirement to generate it algorithmically. The separation asks for one family in VBP_F for which, for every b, some n requires formula size greater than n^b+b. There is no restriction to multilinear computation, bounded depth, homogeneous intermediate gates or noncommuting variables.
cards.answer_criterion: For the stated field F, prove VF_F ⊊ VBP_F by exhibiting a family in VBP_F and proving that its formula sizes are not polynomially bounded, or prove VF_F=VBP_F by showing that every polynomial-size branching-program family has polynomial-size formulas. Any characteristic or field restriction must be stated as part of the scope of the answer. A lower bound only for bounded-depth or multilinear formulas does not resolve the unrestricted question.

cards.definitions: For each n≥1, a property Dₙ is a set of probability distributions on Ωₙ={0,1}ⁿ. It is label-invariant if P∈Dₙ exactly when π_*P∈Dₙ for every bijection π:Ωₙ→Ωₙ, where (π_*P)(y)=P(π^{-1}(y)). This permits arbitrary permutations of all strings, not merely permutations of bit coordinates. For x,y∈Ωₙ let h(x,y)=n^{−1}|{j:xⱼ≠yⱼ}|. Define W_H(P,Q)=min_w Σ_{x,y}w(x,y)h(x,y), where w≥0 has row sums P and column sums Q. The distance to Dₙ is inf_{Q∈Dₙ}W_H(P,Q). A DoHO tester is a randomized algorithm given n and rational ε∈(0,1), with access to independent samples X¹,X²,…∼P. A sample is an oracle for an n-bit string: querying a pair (i,j) reveals only Xⁱⱼ, and further queries to that sample reveal bits of the same string. The algorithm may adapt which sample and coordinate to query. It must accept P∈Dₙ with probability at least 2/3 and reject when inf_{Q∈Dₙ}W_H(P,Q)>ε with probability at least 2/3, with no requirement in the intermediate region. Probability includes samples and internal randomness. It does not compare against total-variation testing in the standard model, where each sample is revealed in full and closeness has a different definition.

cards.definitions: For a fixed arity k and predicate f:{−1,+1}ᵏ→{0,1}, generate M independent constraints on n Boolean spins: each constraint chooses k variable indices independently and uniformly from {1,…,n}, allowing repetitions, and k independent uniform signs. Its value on σ is f(ε₁σᵢ₁,…,εₖσᵢₖ). Write α=M/n for the clause density and v(σ) for the fraction of constraints satisfied. The constant mean is μ=2^{−k}Σₓf(x). For S⊆{1,…,k}, the Fourier coefficient is f̂(S)=2^{−k}Σₓ f(x)∏ⱼ∈S xⱼ. Define aₚ=Σ_{|S|=p}f̂(S)² and ξ(t)=Σ_{p=1}^k aₚtᵖ. The corresponding spin-glass objective is Hξ(σ)=Σ_{p=1}^k √aₚ n^{−(p−1)/2}Σ_{i₁,…,iₚ=1}^n J^{(p)}_{i₁,…,iₚ}σᵢ₁⋯σᵢₚ, with all J entries independent standard normal variables. The CSP improvement over its mean is on the 1/√α scale, whereas Hξ/n has constant-order optimum. For ℓ configurations σ¹,…,σℓ, their full overlap vector Q has one coordinate for every I⊆{1,…,ℓ}: Q_I=n^{−1}Σ_{j=1}^n∏_{i∈I}σⁱⱼ. The empty product is one; two-element I give ordinary pairwise overlaps, and higher-order coordinates must not be discarded. Coupled ensembles permit correlations between instance objectives, as opposed to always taking independently generated instances. The intended comparison takes the large-n limit before the large-density limit; the source does not specify all additional limiting and solution-selection choices.

The substantive target is convergence of the full probability laws of Q, or a refutation under those same conventions. Agreement only of optimal values, attainable overlap supports or forbidden overlap regions does not establish equality of probability laws.

references.title: Extension Preservation in the Finite and Prefix Classes of First Order Logic
references.authors: Dawar, Anuj; Sankaran, Abhisekh
references.locator: Unresolved-question passage on page 12; PDF page 12

cards.definitions: A finite relational vocabulary τ consists of finitely many relation symbols of specified finite arities and finitely many constant symbols, with no positive-arity function symbols. A finite τ-structure A has a finite nonempty domain, interprets each r-ary relation as a subset of A^r, and interprets each constant as an element of A. Equality has its usual meaning. First-order formulas use these atomic predicates and equality, Boolean connectives, and quantifiers ∃x,∀x over the domain; a sentence has no free variables. A formula is in prenex form if a sequence of quantifiers precedes a quantifier-free matrix. Σ_j contains sentences with at most j consecutive blocks of like quantifiers, starting existentially; Π_j is the corresponding universal-starting class. Lower fragments and quantifier-free sentences are included using vacuous padding, valid for nonempty domains. Block lengths are arbitrary finite numbers; k bounds the number of blocks, not the total number of quantifiers. A⊆B means A’s domain is a subset of B’s, every constant has the same interpretation, and each relation of A is exactly the restriction of B’s relation to tuples in A. Thus an extension may add vertices and relations involving new vertices, but cannot change atomic facts on old vertices. The finite models of φ are extension-closed if A⊆B and A⊨φ imply B⊨φ for all finite τ-structures A,B. Equivalence in the finite means A⊨φ iff A⊨ψ for every finite τ-structure A; no equivalence on infinite structures is required. The vocabulary stays fixed when replacing φ by ψ, so no new predicates, constants or built-in order may be added. The question asserts existence of an equivalent sentence, not a uniform translation-time or sentence-length bound.
cards.answer_criterion: Settle the Π_k-collapse assertion and its stronger Σ_{k−1}-collapse version under the stated quantifiers. A positive answer requires a same-vocabulary equivalent sentence for every eligible φ. Refutation of either assertion requires an even k≥4 and a finite vocabulary and extension-closed Σ_k sentence having no equivalent sentence in that target fragment over finite structures. A separation at odd k or one that changes the vocabulary does not settle these assertions.

context_blocks.title: A semantic restriction may reduce quantifier alternation
context_blocks.text: Extension closure says that truth survives adding new elements while preserving the induced structure on old ones. The question asks whether this semantic restriction lets a sentence that starts with existential quantifiers be expressed in a simpler prefix class.

context_blocks.title: The unrestricted classical theorem fails on finite structures
context_blocks.text: When all structures are allowed, extension preservation characterizes existential sentences. Restricting preservation and equivalence to finite structures invalidates that characterization. context_blocks.title: Even and odd levels behave differently in known results

category_assignment.reason: The target is a structural containment theorem for permutation classes of unbounded grid-width. Its pattern-matching application does not make it a string algorithm, and its grid parameter is not an ordinary graph-width question.

importance.reason: Importance has not been individually assessed. This draft shares the provisional midpoint with other unassessed drafts; its position is not evidence that the question is less important.

sentences: Permutation grid classes organize patterns through regions constrained to behave monotonically.
The saved question asks whether every class of unbounded grid-width contains arbitrarily large connected monotone grid subclasses.
Such a structural principle would turn one measure of growing complexity into a concrete family of increasingly large patterns.
It would support the source's broader complexity classification for permutation pattern matching.
The excerpt does not define grid-width or subclass containment conventions, so the proposed implication remains tied to those definitions and is not substituted by an ordinary graph-grid theorem.

methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
